title: Track covered call P&L as one trade with two legs
summary: A covered call is one trade with two legs: long shares and a short call. Count the P&L of both legs together. If you only count the premium from the sold call, you overstate your results, because the shares can lose much more than the premium.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. You own 100 shares and sell one 30-day call at the $105 strike.
The dashed lines are the two legs: long shares and a short call. Each one alone tells only half the story.
The solid line is the whole trade at expiry. This is the P&L you must track.
The gain is capped above $105: the stock gain up to the strike plus the premium.
Breakeven is the purchase price minus the premium. Below it the trade loses money, whatever the premium was.
If the stock falls, the share loss can be many times the premium. Counting only the premium hides this loss.

takeaways: A covered call is one trade. Report the P&L of the shares and the sold call together.
Counting only the call premium as profit is misleading when the shares lose value.
Judge the strategy by the combined result, not by the income line.
caveats: The transcript ends mid-sentence. Strike, price and days in the chart are example values, not from the speaker.
